newsitem.title: QATAR: U.S. air force to hold joint exercises in Qatar.
newsitem.headline: U.S. air force to hold joint exercises in Qatar.

text.p: Thirty U.S. military planes are due to be deployed in Qatar from February 20 to May 20, Qatari and U.S. officials said on Wednesday.

"The goal of the visit is to strengthen the long-term working relationship with Qatar, enhance the coalition fighting skills through training with the Qatar Air Force and flying sorties in support of Operation Southern Watch," a U.S. embassy official said.
Operation Southern Watch enforces a no-fly zone over southern Iraq declared by the United States and other Western powers in 1992.

"The deployment follows consultations between the governments of the state of Qatar and the United States in the context of the bilateral defence agreement," a Qatari Foreign Ministry official told reporters.
Neither the Qatari nor the U.S. official disclosed how many U.S. and Qatari airmen would take part in the exercises or what type of U.S. planes would be deployed.
Oil and gas-rich Qatar signed a defence treaty with the United States after the 1991 Gulf War which liberated Kuwait from Iraqi occupation.
It will be the second deployment of the U.S. Airpower Expeditionary Force to Qatar since last year. Some 34 aircraft were deployed in Qatar from July 3 to September 2.

Qatar, a peninsula on the east coast of Saudi Arabia, is the site of two U.S. military warehouses. Last year the navies and air forces of the two countries held three sets of exercises to train for what they described as "any eventuality".
During the mission, the U.S. force will hold joint exercises with the Qatar Air Force, which is believed to have 18 planes -- all of them French-made Mirage fighter jets.

"The programme intends strictly to strengthen the defence relations between the U.S. and Qatar, demonstrating the U.S. commitment to the state of Qatar's security, and is not aimed against any other party and is non-aggressive in nature," the Qatari official said.
